Similarities between the current setup and April 2025:

Leading into the weekend: Indices dropped 10% over Thursday and Friday. Same thing happened this year.

Monday: In 2025, we were down 5% in pre-market before a big rally to close green. This time, it was a green open and a green close.

Tuesday: Deep red both times, closing at the lows, with tariff talk leading into Wednesday.

Wednesday: Deep red open followed by a reversal both times.

Sentiment: VIX hit 40 and CPC went over 1.2 in both cases.

I feel less confident calling a bottom this time since we’re later in the cycle, but there are definitely some interesting signs (bottom not my base case either)

tweets.quoted_tweet_text:
there is a problem with on-chain deposit volume

we all look at it to find upcoming, trending and the biggest casinos. we judge size and growth by it, affiliates use it to pick deals, streamers use it to pick partners

but a big part of it was never real. let me explain why

here's how deposit volume works:

every player gets a deposit address. they send funds there, the casino sweeps it into its hot wallet, on-chain monitors track every incoming transaction into that hot wallet and count it as volume, done

sounds fine. the problem is everything else that lands in the hot wallet:

- casino top ups and internal infrastructure moving funds around
- exchange transfers sent straight into the hot wallet, no deposit address, no player behind it
- treasury, market maker and other non-player wallets

none of that should count. all of it does

and we've caught casinos inflating their numbers this way. on purpose or not, we can't say. but it happened

so we went through it. 4,500 wallets, manually reviewed

the solution is real deposits. one switch that only counts money coming from actual players

i just put the switch on

toshibet -61%
sportsbetio -52%
betfury -41%
metawin -38%
stakeus -35%. ~$375m gone
thrill -25%. a quarter, in every single timeframe

betfury over the last 7 days: -83%

stake? -4%. roobet, shuffle, 1win, rainbet all single digits

a few million excluded on a multi billion dollar casino doesn't change a thing. but for a small casino, $10m of inflated volume can easily be 50-60% of their total volume, showing triple-digit growth even though they're the same size as a month before

not all of it is shady. maybe someone won big and the casino needed to top up a coin from an exchange. but currently it's all included

deposit volume tells you activity, not who's making money

check it yourself on FairGambling
